title: Conductor agent report, version 1
$comment: Master plan §6.5 and §4.8. THE REPORT IS EVIDENCE, NEVER AUTHORITY: `claim: COMPLETE` with `reconcile() == NO_CHANGE` is CONTRADICTED and a finding (acceptance row 6). This schema exists to make that contradiction machine-detectable, not to be believed. It is the single source for the shape — `conductor_agent::codex::REPORT_SCHEMA_JSON` is this file, via include_str!, so the two cannot drift. Parsed by `conductor_core::report::AgentReport`, which deliberately has no deny_unknown_fields (§2.2: never on anything an agent produced), so a field added by a later Conductor still loads here. STILL v1 AT S13: the five review inputs below are additive and optional, so a report written before they existed still validates and a report carrying them still parses on a build that ignores them. A compatible extension is not a new schema, and bumping `$id` would force every adapter to be told about a change that cannot break any of them.

claim.description: COMPLETE only if the task is finished; PARTIAL if progress was made but work remains; FAILED if the task could not be done.
claim.$comment: §6.5's prose spells these `complete | partial | blocked`. `FAILED` ships instead of `blocked` deliberately: `BLOCKED` is one of §5.2's twelve task states, reached only by Conductor's own eligibility refusal (acceptance row 30), and letting an agent put itself there would conflate a claim with a state Conductor alone may write.

files_touched.description: Every file created, modified or deleted, as a path relative to the workspace root.
files_touched.$comment: §6.5 calls this `files_changed`. Named `files_touched` here because it is a claim, not an observation: §4.8 reads the changed set out of git, and a name matching git's would invite reading this as the answer.

summary.description: One paragraph describing what was changed and why.

task_id.description: The task you were given, echoed back.
task_id.$comment: S13. A cross-check a human reads beside the task Conductor actually launched. Absent and empty are different facts, which is why the Rust field is an Option and this is not in `required`.

commands_run.description: Commands you ran while working on the task.
commands_run.$comment: S13, review input. NOT verification: §4.5's checks are the ones Conductor runs itself, bound to a tree hash. These are a claim, which is why their only consumer is a review packet a human reads and never a completion criterion.

acceptance_criteria.description: Ids of the acceptance criteria you believe you satisfied.
acceptance_criteria.$comment: S13, review input. Evidence for the reviewer's side-by-side, never a substitute for criterion 5's binding: a criterion is satisfied by a passing check, not by being named here.

deviations.description: Anywhere you knowingly departed from the plan, and why.
deviations.$comment: S13, review input, and the most valuable field here for a reviewer: a deviation the agent volunteers is one a human does not have to find in a diff.

blockers.description: Anything that stopped you making further progress.
blockers.$comment: S13, review input. Distinct from a FAILED claim: an agent can finish PARTIAL and still have hit something a human can clear in a minute.

unverified_claims.description: Statements you are making that nothing checked.
unverified_claims.$comment: S13, review input. §4.5's `manual: true` escape hatch forces a review boundary for exactly this class of statement; carrying them explicitly means a reviewer sees 'the agent asserts this and nothing checked it' rather than an unqualified summary.
